unit_attributes.statement: No person maintaining, servicing, repairing, or disposing of an appliance or industrial process refrigeration may knowingly vent or otherwise release into the environment any refrigerant from such appliances, subject to the exemption for specific substitutes in specific end-uses.
unit_attributes.actor: person maintaining, servicing, repairing, or disposing of an appliance or industrial process refrigeration
unit_attributes.actor_quote: person maintaining, servicing, repairing, or disposing of an appliance or industrial process refrigeration

unit_attributes.statement: Notwithstanding any other provision of this subpart, the following substitutes in the following end-uses are exempt from the venting prohibition and from the requirements of this subpart: (i) Carbon dioxide in any application; (ii) Nitrogen in any application; (iii) Water in any application; (iv) Ammonia in commercial or industrial process refrigeration or in absorption units; (v) Chlorine in industrial process refrigeration (processing of chlorine and chlorine compounds); (vi) Hydrocarbons in industrial process refrigeration (processing of hydrocarbons); (vii) Ethane (R-170) in very low temperature refrigeration equipment and equipment for non-mechanical heat transfer; (viii) Propane (R-290) in retail food refrigerators and freezers—stand-alone units; household refrigerators, freezers, and combination refrigerators and freezers; self-contained room air conditioners for residential and light commercial air-conditioning and heat pumps; vending machines; self-contained commercial ice machines, very low temperature refrigeration equipment, and water coolers; and effective July 15, 2024, retail food refrigeration—refrigerated food processing and dispensing equipment; (ix) Isobutane (R-600a) in retail food refrigerators and freezers (stand-alone units only); household refrigerators, freezers, and combination refrigerators and freezers; and vending machines; and (x) R-441A in retail food refrigerators and freezers (stand-alone units only); household refrigerators, freezers, and combination refrigerators and freezers; self-contained room air conditioners for residential and light commercial air-conditioning; heat pumps; and vending machines.

De minimis releases associated with good faith attempts to recycle or recover refrigerants are not subject to the venting prohibition, where (except for exempt substitutes) refrigerant releases are de minimis only if they occur when: (i) the applicable practices in §§ 82.155 and 82.156 are observed, the applicable practices in § 82.157 are observed for appliances that contain any class I or class II refrigerant or blend containing a class I or class II refrigerant, recovery and/or recycling machines that meet the requirements in § 82.158 are used whenever refrigerant is removed from an appliance, the technician certification provisions in § 82.161 are observed, and the reclamation requirements in § 82.164 are observed; or (ii) the requirements in subpart B of this part are observed.
unit_attributes.choice_text: Releases qualify as de minimis only if either condition (i) is satisfied (all specified practices in §§ 82.155, 82.156, and if applicable 82.157, machine requirements under § 82.158, technician certification under § 82.161, and reclamation requirements under § 82.164 are observed) OR condition (ii) is satisfied (requirements in subpart B of this part are observed).

unit_attributes.statement: The knowing release of a class I or class II refrigerant or a non-exempt substitute refrigerant after its recovery from an appliance is a violation of the venting prohibition.

No person may maintain, service, repair, or dispose of an appliance containing a class I or class II refrigerant or a non-exempt substitute refrigerant without both: (1) observing the applicable practices in §§ 82.155, 82.156, and 82.157; and (2) using recovery and/or recycling equipment that is certified for that type of refrigerant and appliance under § 82.158.
